state.misconception_label: Has used slant height and base to find area of a triangle rather than perpendicular height and base

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: How would you calculate the area of this triangle? ![A triangle, base 12m. All three sides are equal.](). I got \( \frac{12 \times 12}{2} \) because I added the side lengths instead of multiplying.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were building a roof with this triangle — would measuring the slant height and base help you figure out how much material you need, or would measuring the perpendicular height and base be more accurate?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess measuring the perpendicular height would be better for figuring out the area, but I thought the slant height was important too. So, if I want to find the area, I should really use the straight height instead of the slant one? How do I find that height if I only have the sides?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were trying to find the height of a tree by measuring the angle it makes with the ground. Would that give you the same accurate height as measuring straight up from the base of the tree?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you're saying about the height being straight up from the base, like how you measure a tree. But if I only have the side lengths, how do I actually find that straight height? Do I need to use some kind of formula or something?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses analogies that gesture toward perpendicular vs. slant height but never directly addresses the student's specific misconception or helps them calculate the actual perpendicular height, leaving the student still asking how to proceed after four turns.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete real-world analogies (building a roof, measuring a tree) to help the student understand the abstract concept of perpendicular height versus slant height in triangle area calculations.
